clue.text: One flying Dublin to Paris must take off with celeb

indicators.note: off signals that the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrity hitches a ride on a flight from Dublin to Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'take off', but it is the anagram signal for MUST, TAKE and CELEB together; 'with' is a link. The Irish writer left Dublin to settle in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish playwright fled Dublin and lived most of his life in Paris, so he is someone who flew from one city to the other.

clue.text: 4 across's day in his post-flight temporary residence

indicators.note: in puts the day word inside the his word

parts.note: son is French for his, the language of the playwright's adopted home
jour is French for day, the language the playwright wrote in

explanation.surface: Beckett spends his days in a temporary home after fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are French, the cue being Beckett's move to Paris and his writing in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A sojourn is a temporary stay somewhere, such as the playwright's stay in France after leaving Ireland.

clue.text: One acting dumb in 1999 TV series

parts.note: 1999 in Roman numerals is MIM (1000 + 1000 less 1)
ER was an American hospital drama series

explanation.surface: An actor plays a mute in a 1999 TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: MIM is a compact (if non-standard) Roman form of 1999.
explanation.definitionFit: A mime artist performs without speaking, so is one acting while dumb.

clue.text: Sitting comfortably? Here, perhaps, is Spooner's popular but second-rate tune

indicators.note: Spooner's means the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: cheesy means popular but trashy
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Someone asks if we are comfortable while a naff tune plays.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEESY AIR becomes EASY CHAIR when its opening sounds are exchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair is a place where one might be sitting comfortably.

clue.text: See 1
Attacks the in-group?

definitions.meaning: in cricket the side that is in is batting

explanation.definitionFit: To batter is to pound; in cricket, the team that is in is made up of batsmen.

clue.text: Group of professionals raced around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A group of professionals raced around.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a core group of trained people, such as officers or activists.

clue.text: Africans say pay isn't bad

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

indicators.note: bad shows the letters are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: African workers complain that their wages are not bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Egyptians are people from Egypt, in north Africa.

clue.text: Party hard after putting rubbish out

indicators.note: out means the rubbish word is placed outside the hard letter

parts.note: trash is rubbish
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Partying hard after taking the rubbish out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after putting' is surface glue; H goes inside TRASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrash is informal for a lively party.

clue.text: Dublin's loveless 21 married a single dying man, according to 4 across

parts.note: lone means single

explanation.surface: Dublin's Molly marries a lone dying man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dublin's loveless 21 married' points to Molly (MOLLOY without O) and her famous Dublin surname; the novel is Malone Dies.
explanation.definitionFit: Beckett's novel Malone Dies centres on Malone, an old man waiting to die.

clue.text: Inventor has to stick ends of loose wires onto power unit

parts.note: to jam is to stick fast

indicators.note: ends of picks the last letter of each of the two following words

parts.note: the watt is the SI unit of power

explanation.surface: An electrician twists the loose wire ends onto a power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: WATT is also the title of a Beckett novel, keeping the theme going.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish engineer famous for improving the steam engine is a celebrated inventor.

clue.text: Drive round town with white goods item

indicators.note: round tells us the Drive abbreviation goes around the town's name

parts.note: Dr is the street-name abbreviation for Drive
Rye is a small town in East Sussex, England

explanation.surface: A motorist drives around a town carrying a fridge or washing machine.
explanation.definitionFit: White goods are large kitchen appliances, and a tumble drier is one of them.

clue.text: Mournful ricercata's Germanic name

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, saying these words contain the name within their letters

explanation.surface: A mournful piece of fugal music bears a Germanic title.
explanation.walkthrough: A ricercata is an early fugue-like instrumental piece; the name runs across the end of 'Mournful' and the start of 'ricercata'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulric is an old Germanic personal name meaning wolf-power.

clue.text: Those panned for endless brawl during fightback

indicators.note: during means the shortened brawl sits inside the fight word

parts.note: a set-to is a fight; written back it gives these letters

indicators.note: endless means the brawl word loses its final letter

parts.note: a melee is a confused brawl

explanation.surface: A scrap breaks out as one side fights back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fightback' hides two ideas: SET-TO for fight, turned backwards to OTTES, into which goes MELE (MELEE minus its last letter).
explanation.definitionFit: Omelettes are cooked in a pan, so they are things that get panned, in a playful passive sense.

clue.text: Tennis player in hospital — back seat casualty

indicators.note: back means the hospital word is written right to left

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital

indicators.note: casualty suggests the seat is wrecked, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lands in hospital as a back-seat passenger after a car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casualty' reads as an injured person but is the anagram signal for SEAT; 'back' turns SAN into NAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilie Nastase is a Romanian tennis player who was world number one in the 1970s.

clue.text: Eg Rugby by Cliff Morgan?

parts.note: rugby is an example of a sport
a scar is a cliff or rocky outcrop

explanation.surface: Cliff Morgan, a Welsh rugby star, appears as a rugby example.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff Morgan was a famous Welsh rugby fly-half, but here Morgan is the British sports car maker; 'by' joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Morgan is a British manufacturer of classic sports cars.

clue.text: Tunnel underground

definitions.meaning: a pedestrian passage under a road
the American name for an underground railway

explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a subway is a pedestrian tunnel; in the US it is the underground railway.

clue.text: Cooked a lamb's leg with squash etc

indicators.note: Cooked suggests the letters are prepared in a new way

explanation.surface: A leg of lamb is roasted with squash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squash' looks like a vegetable but is the racket sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Squash, tennis and similar sports are all games played with a ball.

clue.text: Soap that is used on company car

indicators.note: used on places the last abbreviation after the others

parts.note: RR, Rolls-Royce, stands for a luxury car
ie is the Latin abbreviation id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A bar of soap gets used to wash a company car.
explanation.walkthrough: Corrie is the nickname of Coronation Street, a long-running British TV soap opera set in Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrie is the popular nickname for a long-running British television soap opera.

clue.text: 4 across's mate?

definitions.meaning: a play by the Irish playwright
checkmate comes at the final stage of a chess game

explanation.definitionFit: Endgame is a Beckett play and also the final phase of chess when mate is delivered.

clue.text: Female setter lives on square in US city

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: in puts the lives and square letters inside the US city

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles
is in the sense of exists, lives
S as an abbreviation of square

explanation.surface: A woman setter lives on a square in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Melissa is a woman's first name, so it fits the clue's Female as a female name.

clue.text: 4 across's common name for King Edward?

definitions.meaning: a novel by the Irish playwright
King Edward is a potato variety and ... is slang for potato

explanation.definitionFit: Murphy is a Beckett novel, and an informal word for a potato such as a King Edward.

clue.text: Extremely vigilant girl, brought up right!

indicators.note: brought up in a down entry means written bottom to top

parts.note: Ella is a girl's name
yes, right! as an exclamation of agreement

explanation.surface: A watchful girl was raised properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all eyes means watching intently, fully vigilant.

clue.text: Gangster's girlfriend — only heartless 4 across character

parts.note: a moll is a gangster's girlfriend

indicators.note: heartless removes the inner letters, leaving the outside of the word

explanation.surface: A gangster's girlfriend is the only character without a heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Molloy is the title character of a Beckett novel.

clue.text: Older aunt cooked for foreigner

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are doctored and rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly aunt prepares a meal for a visitor from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlander is a stranger from another land, a foreigner.

clue.text: Artiste was oddly confused

indicators.note: oddly picks letters in odd positions: first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: An artist was strangely bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea means being bewildered or confused.

clue.text: Russian type of dancer meets 25 twice!

parts.note: a go-go dancer performs in clubs
twice 25 is 50, the Roman numeral L

explanation.surface: A Russian go-go dancer meets someone twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' looks like a reference to 25-down but is just the number: doubled it makes 50, Roman L.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol was a Russian writer, author of Dead Souls.

clue.text: 4 across's non-arrival in follow-up books

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word is written upwards

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A Beckett character fails to turn up in a sequel.
explanation.definitionFit: In Waiting for Godot the title character never arrives.

clue.text: Hair in reporter's smoked salmon

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the word, so we want something that sounds like the salmon word

parts.note: lox is cured or smoked salmon, especially in the US

explanation.surface: A hair turns up in a news reporter's smoked salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: Locks are tresses, strands or curls of a person's hair.

clue.text: Maybe he's a lady, maiden admitted, with tail between legs

indicators.note: admitted means the maiden letter is let into the other letters
Maybe suggests the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written, letters HESALADY
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone sheepishly confesses that a man is really a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' puts M (maiden) among the letters of HE'S A LADY; 'Maybe' then shuffles the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog slinks off with its tail between its legs when shamed, so the phrase means in a shamefaced way.

clue.text: Distance driven in police time?

parts.note: Scotland Yard, the London police headquarters
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A distance covered by a police car in a set time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driven' is golf, not motoring: the yardage of a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf yardage is the distance a ball travels, so a drive is measured in yards.

clue.text: In the circumstances, wine is half drunk and half left till later

indicators.text: half drunk and half left till later
indicators.note: half of the word is goes into the wine, swallowed, and the other half stays at the end

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drinker downs half a glass of wine and saves the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The long indicator 'half drunk and half left till later' moves one letter of the second word inside the wine, while the rest stays at the end, as if a drinker sips half and saves half.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the present state of affairs, as things stand.
